name: Choir
description: Wordless voices for held chords: a small section of singers on every note, sung through five formants that morph from Ah through Eh, Ee and Oh to Oo and slowly breathe.

params.name: Vowel
params.description: Which vowel the choir sings, morphing from Ah through Eh, Ee and Oh to Oo.

params.name: Voice
params.description: Size of the singers' vocal tract, from basses at the bottom through men and women to children at the top. The pitch stays the same.

params.name: Motion
params.description: How much the vowel and the size of the voices drift slowly on their own, so a held chord keeps changing colour.

params.name: Breath
params.description: How much breath noise is mixed into the voices. It follows the notes being sung and takes on the vowel.

params.name: Ensemble
params.description: How many singers share each note, from one to three standing left and right, and how far apart they are in pitch and timing.

params.name: Vibrato
params.description: Depth of the singers' vibrato. It arrives a moment after each note starts, the way a singer finds the note first.

params.name: Vibrato Rate
params.description: How fast the vibrato wavers. Each singer's rate is slightly different, so a section does not waver in step.

params.name: Attack
params.description: How long each note takes to fade in. Short is a clear entry; long is a slow swell.

params.name: Release
params.description: How long each note takes to fade out after the key is released.

params.name: Tone
params.description: Low-pass on the voices ahead of the vowel filter. Lower is darker and softer; higher is brighter with more breath and air.

params.name: Width
params.description: How far the singers and the breath spread left and right. At zero the choir is mono.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Output level of the instrument. A soft clip after it rounds off the peaks when many notes stack up.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. A paraphonic formant voice in the manner of the seventies choir machines, with the source and tract of a formant speech synthesiser: KLGLOTT88 glottal pulses (Klatt and Klatt 1990) into five formant resonators in parallel, weighted to equal their cascade. Formant frequencies F1 to F3 are the male averages of Peterson and Barney (1952); F4 and F5 are the 3500 and 4500 Hz of a uniform 17.5 cm tract; bandwidths are those commonly tabulated for a sung tenor, with the first formant of Ee, Oh and Oo widened from 40 Hz to 60-70 Hz. It is not a model of any one instrument or singer.
